description: From August 2019 to January 2020 at least 16 Iranian students were detained and deported after arriving at US airports despite holding valid student visas. Boston Logan was the focal point - at least 10 sent back from August 2019, more than seven through Logan.
source_name: Deportation of Iranian students at US airports

aspect: EXAMPLE - Shahab Dehghani, deported against a court order
description: Dehghani arrived at Logan on 19 January 2020 to study at Northeastern. CBP detained and questioned him for hours then revoked the student visa the State Department had granted after a year of intense vetting. A federal judge issued an emergency stay delaying removal for two days. CBP put him on a flight to Iran anyway. His attorney said he was removed without access to his lawyer and without being told the basis.
money_note: Flights, tuition deposit, legal fees, lost year.
energy_note: A federal court order ignored in real time.

description: A DHS official later told WBUR that CBP denied Dehghani entry because they believed his immediate family had ties to the IRGC, and claimed family ties to a transport company sanctioned in 2010. His attorney denied any grounds of inadmissibility existed.
energy_note: Excluded for his relatives, told only via the press.

description: Crowds gathered at Boston Logan in protest while he was held, which did not stop the removal.

Attorney Susan Church also represented an Iranian student hoping to attend Harvard Divinity School who was denied entry at Logan in 2019. A 35-year-old traveller denied entry in September 2019 had her visa revoked and was placed on a removal flight.
Iranians turned away at the US border rose more than 150% from 2015 to 2019 - 736 to 1,895 - even as Iranian student and exchange visitors fell 43%. More refusals from a smaller pool.
A CBP spokesman said less than one percent of Iranian passengers arriving at Boston were deported in 2019 - a denominator chosen to make the number small.

aspect: It kept going under a new administration
description: A January 2021 Boston Globe investigation found the practice continuing via expedited removal, with Logan a hotbed of litigation over these cases.

aspect: The lawyers think the count is higher
description: The AILA New England chair suggested the real number could be as high as two dozen, because deportations are not always public.

aspect: Expedited removal carries a five-year bar
description: Removal at the border is not simply being sent home - expedited removal normally triggers a multi-year bar on return, so a single airport decision closes the country for years.
energy_note: One officer, one shift, five years.
